analyst_view.overall: Club Brugge (11th) and Liverpool (10th) are level on 9 points, so the winner moves close to the top eight. Brugge have won their last three in Europe and won 5-1 at Mechelen on Saturday; Joel Ordonez is out and winger Jan Virgili a doubt, both counted by the numbers. Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 on Sunday; Gakpo and Gravenberch are out (counted) along with Ekitike (counted), Leoni and Bradley, and one injury list today also has Jeremie Frimpong out with a muscle bruise, which the numbers don't list, although the same page still has him in its predicted XI. Spanish referee Alejandro Hernandez Hernandez gives a lot of cards and the numbers already add about 29% to cards for him.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, split evenly, already taking off Ekitike (-8.3%) and Gakpo and counting both sides' scoring runs. Liverpool still have Isak, Wirtz and Barcola, and Brugge have been scoring freely at home; Frimpong's reported knock touches the wing more than the scoring, so I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, 6.2 for Liverpool. Without Gakpo and possibly Frimpong, Liverpool's width comes from Barcola and Szoboszlai, which still pushes play wide, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already adding about 29% for Hernandez Hernandez's high card rate. It is a close game with a lot at stake but no rivalry, and nothing new on discipline turned up, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 35.0 shots, already lifted for both sides' heavy recent shooting (+15% and +19%). Both teams press and attack, and the absences are counted, so I stay at 35.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.8 on target, with both sides' recent accuracy counted. Liverpool's main finishers bar Ekitike and Gakpo are fit and Brugge's Tresoldi is in form, so I stay at 11.8.
